roleTitle: Software Quality Engineer, Retail Store Operations
jobDescription: Store operations at a regional grocery chain run a store-task application on handheld devices in every store. The Software Quality Engineer owns quality for the application end-to-end, decides the test scope for each release, holds the sign-off before a release goes to stores, and is accountable to the head of store systems for defects reaching stores.
requirements: Owns application quality end-to-end and holds the sign-off before each release goes to stores.
Maintains the automated test suite for the store-task application on the handheld device fleet.
Runs the pilot-store test rounds with store staff and records outcomes.
Coordinates release readiness with the development lead and store operations and records own responsibility boundaries.
Documents known limitations and hand-over conditions for each store release.

evidence.text: Maintained the automated test suite for the store-task application on the handheld fleet (Appium against the two device models in use), adding the offline-sync scenarios after a store outage.
Ran the pilot-store test rounds with store staff in three pilot stores before each release, recording outcomes per scenario and escalating blocking defects to the development lead.
Prepared the release readiness summary for the store systems manager, who decided the test scope with the development lead and gave the sign-off for the release to go to stores.
Wrote the release notes for store operations, listing known limitations (the task-photo feature needed the newer device model) and the hand-over items for the store support desk.
Responsibilities included suite maintenance, pilot-store rounds, readiness summaries and release notes for the store-task application over about two years, reporting to the store systems manager.
Work sample: the Appium suite's scenario list and one pilot-store round's results sheet, with the device-farm run identifiers as a verification trail.

Hiring manager pre-read: the candidate's CV cover note says he was 'accountable for store release quality end-to-end'; the head of store systems wants exactly that, so the packet must show what accountability he actually held.
Reference call with the former store systems manager: said the candidate 'knew the app better than anyone' and that she 'never had to overrule his readiness summary'; confirmed employment dates.

propositions.text: The candidate maintained the Appium test suite for the store-task application on the handheld fleet and added the offline-sync scenarios.
propositions.rationale: The resume and the scenario list document the suite.

propositions.text: The candidate ran pilot-store test rounds with store staff in three pilot stores and recorded outcomes per scenario.
propositions.rationale: The resume and the results sheet document the pilot rounds.

propositions.text: The candidate was accountable for store release quality end-to-end and held the release sign-off.
propositions.rationale: The resume assigns scope decisions and the sign-off to the store systems manager; the cover-note wording and the referee's praise do not record an authority held.

signatures: knew the app better than anyone

gold.expectedGap: The materials show suite maintenance, pilot rounds and readiness summaries; they do not show the candidate deciding scope or signing releases off.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Keep the boundary the resume states: scope and sign-off by the store systems manager; the candidate tested and summarised.
followUpTargets: Ask whether the candidate ever signed off a store release himself and which readiness decisions were his.
